qt: to the Commission Massimiliano Smeriglio (S&D), Brando Benifei (S&D), Camilla Laureti (S&D), Pina Picierno (S&D), Pietro Bartolo (S&D), Patrizia Toia (S&D), Franco Roberti (S&D), Alessandra Moretti (S&D), Achille Variati (S&D), Beatrice Covassi (S&D), Daniela Rondinelli (S&D) Subject:

On 7 January 2024, in an interview with the newspaper La Repubblica, Federico Mollicone, President of the Committee on Culture, Science and Education in the Chamber of Deputies of the Italian Parliament, said that the government was working on a proposal to amend the Consolidated Act on audiovisual and radio media services (TUSMAR1) in order to 'substantiate the veracity of news stories'. According to the statements made, the aforementioned media reform proposal has been proposed in order to protect journalism, in particular the reliability of sources and the accuracy of information following the 'drift towards sensationalism in the press'. Given the above, can the Commission respond to the following questions: 1.
Is it aware of these statements?

Does it consider that such a reform proposal would be in line with the agreement reached between Parliament and the Council on the Media Freedom Act? Does it not consider that such a proposal, by regulating the choices made by editors, would restrict freedom of the press and freedom of expression?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.2.2024) The Commission is aware of the case referred to by the Honourable Members from media reports. The Commission attaches great importance to upholding and fostering free, pluralistic and independent media, which are essential assets for a functioning democracy, given their key role to help citizens in making informed decisions. Once formally adopted, the European Media Freedom Act1 will require Member States to respect the editorial freedom and independence of media service providers and to refrain from interfering in their editorial activity. The Commission cannot take a position on preliminary proposals.
